awd_titl_txt: Conference: Mathematical Fellowships for the Annual International Conference on Quantum Information Processing (QIP) 2025
awd_abstract_narration:
The 28th Annual Quantum Information Processing Conference (QIP 2025), the premier international conference on the theory of quantum information science, is co-hosted by Duke University and NC State University in Raleigh, North Carolina, from February 24–28, 2025. This conference serves as a global platform for researchers in quantum computing, cryptography, quantum foundations, information theory, and many-body physics to present and discuss groundbreaking advancements. Despite the critical role of mathematics in quantum information science, U.S.-based mathematicians are currently less represented in the QIP community, hindering opportunities for broader interdisciplinary collaboration. To address this, the project provides 40 fellowships for U.S.-based students and early-career researchers in the mathematical sciences. These fellowships align directly with the NSF mission by fostering the progress of quantum information science, strengthening the workforce, and driving innovation in a field with broad societal and technological implications.

Quantum information science has deep ties to mathematics, with foundational contributions from applied and computational mathematics, algebra, analysis, and probability among others. This project supports the participation of U.S.-based students and early-career researchers in the mathematical sciences by providing 40 travel fellowships to attend QIP 2025. The fellowships aim to empower talented young mathematicians to engage in cutting-edge research and interdisciplinary interaction opportunities with quantum information science researchers from other disciplines. Fellows will benefit from research talks, poster sessions, rump sessions, industrial sessions, networking opportunities, and interdisciplinary exposure, significantly advancing their professional development. Ultimately, this initiative supports the development of the next generation of quantum researchers, advancing the field and contributing to the NSF mission.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
This project supported the participation of early-career researchers in mathematical sciences at the International Conference on Quantum Information Processing (QIP) 2025, the premier annual meeting in quantum information science. A total of 45 fellowships were awarded, including 10 postdoctoral scholars or early-career assistant professors, and 35 students, representing 27 universities across 17 U.S. states. The fellowships reduced financial barriers and allowed these researchers to engage directly with the quantum scientific community at a formative stage in their careers.

Fellows actively participated in technical sessions, tutorials, poster presentations, and informal research discussions throughout the conference. QIP also hosted an industrial session, a rump session highlighting emerging ideas, and multiple networking events. These activities provided early-career researchers with valuable scientific exposure and opportunities to connect with experts from academia, national laboratories, and industry. Such experiences help young scholars refine their research directions, build collaborations, and develop the professional skills needed in the rapidly evolving field of quantum information science.

From the perspective of intellectual merit, the project strengthened the engagement of mathematical scientists in quantum information research. Many theoretical advances in quantum algorithms, learning theory, and information theory rely on tools from mathematical sciences. By supporting the participation of mathematicians, the project helped bring rigorous mathematical approaches into conversations that shape the future of quantum information science. In terms of broader impacts, the project contributed to the development of the next generation of researchers in mathematics and quantum science. The fellows’ conference participation enhanced their research training and improved their access to scientific resources, mentorship, and professional networks. These outcomes support the long-term growth of the U.S. quantum research ecosystem and strengthen national leadership in quantum information science.
